_comment: Every scan fixture (tools/make-scan-fixtures.js) and what Check my files should do with it. 'committed' fixtures are in this folder in git; the rest are written fresh each run and gitignored (the header comment in make-scan-fixtures.js says why each one can't be committed). 'windowsOnly' fixtures are written on Windows alone, because what they test (an NTFS file attribute) doesn't exist elsewhere.

fixtures.note: real text, not scanned: wages, a made-up SSN and EIN
made-up site logins, an AWS-style key and a phone number
a cell with a made-up card number, and a cell comment with another made-up detail (not read yet: attachments.js's OFFICE_PART doesn't cover xl/comments*.xml)
a made-up place (the Eiffel Tower) in its EXIF GPS
three folders deep: nesting, a made-up email and phone number
no extension at all, named exactly as ssh-keygen leaves it: a made-up OpenSSH private key, plus the same made-up AWS key as logins.txt so the same detail shows up in two files
a made-up /Encrypt reference in its trailer: locked, so 'weren't read', never counted as clean
the browser fixtures' own image-only page (make-picture-fixtures.js's pdf({ scanned: true })): a picture of a page, no text layer, so 'weren't read' names it a scan
Office's own password wrapper (the Compound File Binary magic bytes), never a zip: locked, so 'weren't read'
budget.xlsx cut short before its own central directory: damaged, so 'weren't read'
21 MB: over the picture cap (20 MB); counted, never read. Written under tests/e2e/output/scan/, not here: kept out of apps/ so it never trips the "no AI inside" rule check's big-file guard
the hidden attribute; never counted or opened
the system attribute; never counted or opened
inside a build folder; never opened, never even looked inside
a directory junction back to this folder itself (a link loop); never followed
